what_its_for: Ivermectin is used to treat certain parasitic infections. The tablet form treats infections caused by parasitic worms such as intestinal strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis (river blindness). The cream form (Soolantra) treats rosacea on the face. The lotion form (Sklice) treats head lice. Your doctor will tell you exactly which infection or condition you are being treated for.
how_to_take: Take ivermectin TABLETS on an empty stomach with a full glass of water (at least 8 ounces). Do not eat or drink anything except water for at least 1 hour before and 1 hour after taking the tablet. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it. For the CREAM or LOTION, apply only to the skin area your doctor directed. Do not swallow the cream or lotion. Keep it away from your eyes, mouth, and nose.
dosing: The dose depends on your body weight, the type of infection, and the form of ivermectin you are using. Your doctor will calculate the right dose for you. For most worm infections, you may only need a single dose. For some conditions, you may need to take it again after a few weeks or months. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store ivermectin tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking ivermectin with food, as this can increase the amount of drug absorbed into your body and raise your risk of side effects — always take it on an empty stomach. Avoid alcohol while taking ivermectin, as it may worsen dizziness or lightheadedness. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, because it can cause dizziness or vision changes. Do not use ivermectin to prevent or treat COVID-19 — it has NOT been proven safe or effective for that purpose. Do not share this medication with anyone else.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe skin rash, hives, or itching; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; difficulty breathing or swallowing; chest pain or fast heartbeat; severe dizziness or fainting; confusion or difficulty walking; seizures; severe eye pain, redness, or vision changes; or signs of a serious reaction called Mazzotti reaction (fever, rash, swollen lymph nodes, rapid heartbeat, or low blood pressure). Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse after treatment.
when_it_works: For parasitic worm infections, the medication starts killing the parasites quickly, but you may not feel better right away. It may take several days to weeks before you notice full improvement in your symptoms. Follow-up stool tests or blood tests may be needed to confirm the infection is gone. For rosacea cream, you may start to see improvement in your skin within a few weeks, but full benefit may take up to 3 months of regular use. For head lice lotion, a single application is usually enough to kill lice.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Ivermectin is generally not recommended during pregnancy, especially during the first trimester. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Small amounts of ivermectin can pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using this medication if you are breastfeeding. CHILDREN: Ivermectin tablets are generally not recommended for children weighing less than 33 pounds (15 kg). The head lice lotion (Sklice) can be used in children 6 months and older. Always follow your doctor's guidance for children. ELDERLY: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness. Use with caution and report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. LIVER DISEASE: If you have liver problems, tell your doctor before taking ivermectin, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
